text:
Only refundAgent has a store configured, so orderAgent and triage are client-managed agents that rely on the client passing back snapshotId/state rather than being resumable by sessionId from server storage—this means any frontend expecting to resume via session id would fail for those two.

In the scenario where a customer references an order then follows up asking about its status in the same conversation picked up by session id, triage delegates to orderAgent, but since neither has a store, the session can't be reloaded—it's lost, producing "session not found" and forcing a restart, while single-turn questions still work fine since they don't need resuming. The root cause looks like a missing `store` on orderAgent and triage in agents.ts, so the fix is adding store to both so sessions persist and resume correctly; I should also check how the `agents` middleware propagates sessions during delegation to see if it needs its own store too.

Sub-agents like orderAgent get invoked fresh each delegation since triage's conversation already holds the history and re-passes context, so their own statefulness isn't what matters for resumption. The real entity that needs persisting for session-based resumption is triage itself, since it's the top-level entry point the client reconnects to.

Since triage has no `store` configured, its session lives only in-memory for that single call and is never saved to disk - so when the client tries to resume by sessionId later, there's nothing to load and the conversation has to start over. That matches the bug: first turn works, but reconnecting for the follow-up fails. The fix is to add the same `FileSessionStore` already used for refundAgent to triage as well.

I need to pinpoint the exact broken line in the triage agent definition - likely the `use: [agents({...})]` line that's missing a `store,` entry right after it - and make that edit.

The root cause is clear: triage has no store configured, so when the follow-up "What is its status?" comes in, there's no session history to resolve the order id. Since refundAgent already demonstrates the correct pattern with `store,` in its config and the interface supports it directly on defineAgent, I just need to add that same field to triage's definition.

Root cause located: `triage` is the agent the customer actually chats with, but unlike `refundAgent` it has no `store` configured, so its session is never persisted — a later request that tries to resume the conversation by session id has nothing to load, forcing the customer to restart. `orderAgent`, which `triage` delegates to, is invoked statelessly per delegation anyway, so `triage` is the agent that needs persistence.

text: Fixed `src/agents.ts`: the `triage` agent (the customer-facing entry point for the support chat) had no `SessionStore`, unlike `refundAgent`. Without a store, an agent is client-managed — there's no server-side snapshot, so resuming by session id (via `loadChat`/`getSnapshot`) has nothing to load, forcing the customer to restart. Added the already-defined `store` (the `FileSessionStore` used by `refundAgent`) to `triage` so the "A-1001" → "What is its status?" follow-up can resume correctly. `answer.json` is written at the project root; no dependencies or `package.json` changes were made.
